facts.big: The project was finished on time
facts.label: Passivo no passado
facts.sub: Use was/were + particípio para dizer o que foi feito. Acrescente by + pessoa quando precisar. Pergunte com Was it…? e Were they…?

facts.label: foi, foram + particípio
facts.sub: Use was com um só (The project was finished) e were com vários (The files were lost). Depois coloque o particípio: finished, lost, picked, made, written. É o passivo no passado.

facts.label: por + pessoa
facts.sub: Use by quando quiser dizer quem fez a ação: It was made by Carla. Se a pessoa não importa ou já é óbvia, você pode omitir o by: The grades were posted.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “o projeto foi terminado” ou “terminaram o projeto”.
compare.us: Em inglês, o passivo mostra o que aconteceu com algo: The project was finished. Use was/were + particípio. Com coisas no plural, use were: The files were lost.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: The poster was picked.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The report was written again is passive.
We say The files was lost.
items.why: Files is plural: The files were lost.

items.s: By + person says who did the action.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The report was written again is passive. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say The files was lost. → Falso (Files is plural: The files were lost.)
By + person says who did the action. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A classroom in Portland · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a gray Monday in Portland. Rui walks into the classroom with a big poster. The projects were due last week. Fay sits near the window. The teacher is not in the room yet. The two friends compare their work.

“Rui, was your project finished on time?” says Fay. “Yes, it was finished on Sunday night and handed in on Monday morning.” says Rui. “Mine was late. My files were lost when the computer broke.” says Fay.
